name: Adaptive Thermal Comfort
citation: de Dear, R.J. & Brager, G.S. (1998). Developing an adaptive model of thermal comfort. ASHRAE Transactions, 104(1), 145-167.

constructs.description: Deviation from interoceptive thermal set-point generates PE. Set-point is adaptable, not fixed (contra Fanger PMV).
Occupant agency: window opening, clothing changes, activity modulation. EC affordances enable thermal self-regulation.
Vasomotor adjustment, acclimatization. Body calibrates thermal expectations over time.
Explicit frame (IE-DPT) shifts thermal expectation in NV buildings. NV selection → recalibrated expectations → wider comfort band.

irreducible_residual.narrative: Fanger's PMV model fails in naturally ventilated buildings because it ignores the explicit channel entirely. NV building selection (IE-DPT) → recalibrated thermal expectations (IC) → narrower interoceptive PE for wider temperature ranges → wider comfort band. The allesthesia mechanism (thermal pleasure from homeostatic correction) reveals that extreme temperatures can be pleasurable when explicitly expected and desired.

Thermal adaptation is constitutively relevant: intervening on perceived control, building type (natural ventilation vs AC), and prior thermal history directly changes comfort set-point and acceptable temperature range. Design guidance is specific and actionable: HVAC design with personal control, natural ventilation windows, clothing adjustability, and activity modulation all produce measurable comfort band widening.
